story_title: As an Event Coordinator, I want to confirm an event once its essential arrangements are completed so that the Event Organiser can view the confirmed arrangements

acceptance_criteria.text: The Coordinator can confirm an event only when required arrangements have been completed.
The required arrangements are those essential to that particular event.
Given a required arrangement is still incomplete, when the Coordinator attempts to confirm the event, then confirmation is refused and the incomplete arrangement is identified.
Only the assigned Event Coordinator can confirm the event.
A confirmed event has a Confirmed status.
Confirmed venue and equipment arrangements remain associated with the event.
The Event Organiser can view the confirmed event information.

Logged in as Event Coordinator Daniel Tan (daniel.tan@connectsphere.com / password123). This case changes the event's status — SPM-34-TC02 and SPM-34-TC03 read the result, so go straight to those and run npm run fixtures:spm34 after TC03.
steps: Click 'SPM34 Ready To Confirm' in the list
test_cases.test_data:
Event: SPM34 Ready To Confirm (Planning)
Venue: Orchard Seminar Room, booking Approved
Equipment: Handheld Wireless Mic, Reserved
Coordinator: Daniel Tan

Step 2: The event opens with the status badge 'Planning' and a 'Confirm event' button in the header.

Step 4: The message 'The event is confirmed. The organiser can now see the arrangements.' is shown and the status badge changes to 'Confirmed'.

open_questions: RESOLVED 2026-10-03. AC2 originally carried a second clause - 'an arrangement the Coordinator has marked as not required (see: Track Outstanding Arrangements) does not block confirmation'. It was removed from SPM-34 because it duplicates AC10 of Track Outstanding Arrangements, which also owns the mechanism for marking an arrangement not required (its AC7). No requirement was lost; the behaviour is stated once, in the story that builds it. What remains of AC2 - required arrangements are those essential to that particular event - is derived from the event (a venue always, per session; equipment only where a requirement was recorded) and is covered by SPM-34-TC04. When that story lands it sets `required: false` on the arrangement in src/lib/eventConfirmation.ts rather than adding a second rule; note also that its AC2 (several bookings for one event, SPM-81) will need arrangementsFor() to list each booking instead of collapsing them, and its AC8 needs a marker for an arrangement that may not be waived.

Completeness is strict (decided 2026-10-03): a venue booking must be Approved and equipment must be Reserved or Partially fulfilled. A pending venue request does not count (SPM-34-TC07), because it is a question Venue Staff have not answered — confirming on the strength of it is the double-booking the brief warns about (#35, #80). Confirm this is the customer's intent, or ask at the next Q&A whether a pending request should be enough.

Technical support staffing is not checked. The brief lists technical support as an arrangement an event may need (Technical Staff Assignment), but nothing in the system assigns staff to an event, so confirmation cannot test for it. If that story is built, it becomes a third arrangement in src/lib/eventConfirmation.ts.

RESOLVED 2026-10-03: AC4 needed no new rule. canSetEventStatus() already limits the move to Confirmed to the assigned coordinator (STATUS_TRANSITION_ROLES), and the route checks it before the arrangements are read — so an unassigned coordinator is refused on the assignment, never told what is outstanding. SPM-34 added canConfirmEvent() only to decide whether to show the button.
RESOLVED 2026-10-03: no case covers confirming from a status other than Planning. canTransition() already refuses it and SPM-27 tests the lifecycle graph, so a case here would duplicate that.

Raised while validating SPM-34-TC03. The Venue tab is a coordinator's planning screen and is not offered to an Event Organiser; typing its address as the organiser gives the generic 'Could not load this event's booking requests.' rather than an access-denied state, because GET /api/events/[id]/venue-bookings is restricted to the coordinator. SPM-34 therefore puts the booked room on the Overview instead, which is where the organiser already looks. Worth deciding separately whether that tab should be hidden from the organiser outright, or show the refusal properly - the same pattern SPM-22 raised for the Equipment tab.
